title: Environment Access Blueprint — hosted/dedicated/private
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working blueprint defines recommended IAM role constructs, environment-specific access rules, and evidence-automation mappings to support RBAC v2 across Redwood Inference environments: hosted (multi-tenant), dedicated (reserved capacity), and private (VPC/on-prem). It is intended for security engineers, platform engineers, and product owners who will implement or audit access controls.

Guiding principles (short):
- Principle of least privilege by default; grant role-intent not raw permissions.
- Segregation of duties (SoD) between deployment, billing, and security ops.
- Short-lived elevated access and Just-In-Time (JIT) approval for high-risk operations.
- Environment parity where possible, explicit divergence where required by risk/regulation.
- All privileged actions must generate structured audit events (see schema mapping).

High-level role constructs (RBAC v2 primitives):
- Role types: viewer, operator, deployer, infra-operator, security-analyst, billing-admin, support-operator, model-admin, key-rotation, audit-reader.
- Role attributes: environment-scoped (hosted|dedicated|private), resource-scope (org|project|resource-group), session-duration (minutes), approval-bound (boolean).
- Grants should be expressed as role-assignments to groups (SSO groups) not individual accounts.

Environment-by-environment role matrix (recommendations):
Note: Each cell lists recommended owners for role assignment and additional constraints.
1) Hosted (multi-tenant)
- Viewer: engineering-readonly-group; no ability to list secrets.
- Operator: hosted-operator-group; can restart services, view metrics; cannot deploy customer-facing models.
- Deployer/Model-Admin: limited to CI principal with signed commits and branch protection; deploys go through canary workflow only.
- Billing-Admin: finance+accounts-payable group; read-only on usage metrics, no deploy rights.
- Security-Analyst: sec-ops group; read audit logs, create alerts; access via SSO with MFA.
- Key-Rotation: platform-key-admin; only for platform-managed keys; rotation requires two-person approval for KMS ops.

2) Dedicated (customer-dedicated capacity)
- Viewer: dedicated-customer-readonly group (customer SSO mapping possible).
- Operator: infra-operator-dedicated; can scale node pools and adjust autoscaling policies.
- Deployer/Model-Admin: customer-deployer role (scoped to their dedicated pool); must be explicitly approved by CSM and infra.
- Billing-Admin: account-billing-role tied to contract; read usage; cannot change infra config.
- Security-Analyst: sec-ops can be given read access to audit logs but require documented NDA for data access.
- Key-Rotation: for private KMS integrations, rotation is customer-driven; platform provides rotation hooks but does not hold keys.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem)
- Viewer: local-admin-readonly; minimal platform telemetry forwarded by customer-configured collectors.
- Operator: site-infra-operator; operations are jointly performed with customer systems team.
- Deployer/Model-Admin: customer-local-deployer; recommended to use ephemeral service accounts and signed artifacts.
- Billing-Admin: typically not applicable; if present, siloed billing view only.
- Security-Analyst: access only to metadata and platform events; raw customer data not accessible without explicit contract.
- Key-Rotation: customer-controlled HSM/KMS; platform exposes rotation API but requires customer key authorization.

Suggested IAM policy templates (high-level pseudo snippets):
- Read-only viewer (platform): allow: [ListMetrics, GetModelMetadata, ListRoutes]; deny: [AccessSecrets, Decrypt].
- Deployer (scoped): allow: [CreateDeployment, UpdateDeployment] where resource.project = ${project} and source.commit_signature = true; enforce: require-mfa, session_duration <= 60m.
- Infra-operator (higher risk): allow: [ScalePool, ReplaceNode] but require: approval_ticket in ticketing-system and audit tag on request.
(These should be expanded into actual IAM JSONs by infra team; avoid broad wildcard permissions.)

Evidence automation & audit log schema mapping (required fields):
All privileged API events must emit a structured audit record with at least the following fields. Map these to SIEM export columns and ensure ingestion preserves them:
- event_time (ISO8601)
- event_id (UUID)
- actor_id (SSO user id or service principal id)
- actor_principal_type (user|service|api_key)
- actor_groups (list)
- action (string: e.g., CreateDeployment, RotateKey)
- resource_type (e.g., model, deployment, key, capacity-pool)
- resource_id (arn-like identifier)
- environment (hosted|dedicated|private)
- request_id / trace_id
- outcome (success|failure|denied)
- ip_address
- user_agent
- approval_reference (ticket id or null)
- policy_version (rbac-v2 version)
- raw_request (redacted)

SIEM export notes: export should be newline-delimited JSON; include schema_version and source_system tags. Ensure events with sensitive payloads have data redaction flags and that SIEM retains the redaction metadata.

Evidence automation play (automation examples):
- On role assignment to a high-privilege role (infra-operator, key-rotation): emit event role_assignment.created -> SIEM alert + create ticket (if not already present), require 2nd-level approval within 24 hours.
- On create/modify of dedicated/private KMS bindings: emit ksm-bind-change event with approval_reference and snapshot of previous binding.
- On failed deployment attempts with privilege escalation: create security incident draft with aggregated events and add to triage queue.

Detecting misuse: SIEM query examples (pseudo-SQL for rules):
- High-frequency role grants: SELECT actor_id, count(*) as grants FROM audit_events WHERE action = 'AssignRole' AND role IN ('infra-operator','key-rotation') GROUP BY actor_id HAVING grants > 3 OVER 24h
- Suspicious deploy after failed auth: SELECT * FROM audit_events WHERE action = 'CreateDeployment' AND outcome = 'success' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM audit_events e2 WHERE e2.actor_id = audit_events.actor_id AND e2.action = 'Authenticate' AND e2.outcome = 'failure' AND e2.event_time > audit_events.event_time - INTERVAL '10 minutes')

Operational controls and workflows (recommended):
- Provisioning: SSO group -> IAM role mapping. Use automated reconciliation jobs to detect drift nightly and emit drift events.
- JIT elevated access: provide ephemeral session tokens via approval workflow with enforced session duration and audit annotation.
- Key rotations: automated notifications + artifact snapshots (policy and binding), require recorded approval for KMS rotations.
- Dedicated capacity onboarding: ensure customer contract flags required access divergence (e.g., no platform security-analyst direct access).

Migration checklist for RBAC v2 rollout (minimal):
1) Inventory existing roles and permissions; map to RBAC v2 primitives.
2) Create SSO group naming standards and automated provisioning scripts.
3) Deploy audit log schema changes in staging; forward to test SIEM index.
4) Run reconciliation job and generate a migration report (diffs).
5) Pilot with one low-risk service and one dedicated customer; collect telemetry for 2 weeks.
6) Iterate policies and then roll out org-wide.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to represent cross-environment operator roles where on-call must access both hosted and dedicated without excessive privileges? (proposal: environment-limited roles with cross-env escalation tickets).
- Define exact policy JSON templates for platform infra team to adopt (work item assigned: jira:SEC-1342).
- Finalize SIEM index naming, retention, and PII redaction policy in collaboration with privacy team.

Appendix: quick reference of role names to SSO groups (examples)
- sec-analyst -> sso:sec-ops@redwood.example.com
- infra-operator -> sso:infra-ops@redwood.example.com
- hosted-deployer -> github-actions@redwood-ci
- dedicated-customer-deployer -> mapped to customer SSO group

Notes to reviewers: this is a draft blueprint focused on pragmatic constraints for our three environments. Please review for missing controls and provide any contractual differences needed for customers in regulated industries.

References and links: confluence:SEC-RBAC-v2-001, jira:SEC-1342, github:infra/privilege-migration#38
